claim: Toulmin/Pollock/Dung lineage: a conclusion is valid if it survives criticism; attacks come as rebut (contradict conclusion), undercut (attack the inference/warrant) and undermine (attack premise). ASPIC+ formalises this with rationality postulates.
schema_part: G (keep conclusions open to challenge) / O (challenge operator)
agent_test: Require explicit warrant, exception and undercutter slots in the answer trace; compare error rates against plain CoT at equal tokens on exception-laden items.

claim: Burden of proof is a separate parameter from argument strength: three burdens (production, persuasion, tactical) and proof standards (scintilla, best argument, dialectical validity, preponderance, beyond reasonable doubt) change the outcome on the same arguments.
schema_part: S (test state) / G (state who must prove what)
agent_test: Add a field 'who bears burden, which standard' before verdict; test on items where the default answer flips when the burden is moved.

claim: Humans do not follow one abstract semantics. Reinstatement is judged weaker than an unattacked argument: ratings fell from M=5.61 (base) to 5.21 (reinstated), N=103, t(102)=4.636, p<.001. Grounded semantics predicted 0-2.5% of responses in Cramer and Guillaume, preferred/CF2 97-100%, but context (news vs science) changed acceptance 67.5% vs 27.5%.
agent_test: Not an agent test; design warning: do not force the agent to a single Dung semantics, log which one a task needs.

claim: Which abstract semantics describes human judgment (CF2, preferred, grounded, or only 'void precedence') is contested across the lab studies (N=20 original, N=45/60/25 Cramer, N=103 Bezou).
agent_test: None needed.

claim: Generic default reasoning: the best frontier LLMs reach about 96% zero-shot (Claude 3 Opus 96.51, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 96.01, GPT-4 0613 93.52 per the table), but spread is wide (GPT-3.5 48%, 7 models near chance).
agent_test: Re-run a 20-pattern generic default battery on our model at temperature 0 as a baseline.

claim: Chain-of-thought hurts default reasoning in many models: mean drop -11.14% (SD 15.74) for models above 75% zero-shot; deltas -16.28 (Claude 3 Sonnet), -12.62 (GPT-4 0613), -18.77 (Gemini Flash), -33.22 (Yi 34B); a few gain (GPT-4o +4.98). Boundary: DERELAB (2026, different task) finds extended thinking removes the confirmation gap in Qwen3-32B (0.670 to 0.008), so the CoT penalty is task-specific, not general.
schema_part: O (do not force long reasoning on default/exception items) / G
agent_test: Run the same default-reasoning items with and without CoT at equal tokens; if CoT lowers accuracy, route such items to a short direct path plus an exception check.

claim: Models tend to treat generics as universal statements or fail to separate defeasible from deductive inference; 'no impact' is over-predicted (GPT-4 predicts it on 60% of items) and the word 'not' drives 'weakens' predictions. Best macro-F1 on strengthen/weaken/no-impact is only 0.64.
agent_test: After drafting, ask which stated rule is a default and what exception would defeat it; measure on the Allaway-McKeown pattern set.

claim: Accuracy on conflict resolution falls as conflict rate, depth and chain length grow (BoardgameQA at conflict 0.0-0.8; linear attack graphs of 1-25 arguments: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 77.32, GPT-4o 72.31, GPT-4o-mini 54.38, others near 50% at large size).
agent_test: Compare an explicit in/out/undecided label table against free CoT on attack graphs of 5, 15, 25 arguments.

claim: Models not trained on explanations do poorly at computing grounded extensions (Llama3-8B 0.18, GPT-3.5 0.15, GPT-4o 0.54); fine-tuning with explanations reaches 0.95-0.97, and without explanations accuracy can fall to 30% beyond 25 arguments. Large-graph ablation (n 26-35): answer-only 0.68/0.56 (Qwen2.5) vs with intermediate steps 0.85/0.78; this is fine-tuning, no inference-time table was tested.
agent_test: Scaffold analogue: require an explicit step-by-step labelling trace and compare with answer-only at equal tokens.

claim: Non-linear attack graphs expose shortcuts: 'yes' is correct only 8.85% of the time, so 86.81 accuracy (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) hides recall 38.15.
agent_test: Report recall/MCC, not accuracy, on argument-resolution items.

claim: Exception chains (A unless B unless C) break frontier LLMs in a reproducible but unstable way: Claude Opus 4.6 spacecraft 61/68 (89.7%) then 98.5% a month later; GPT-5.4 construction insurance 96.6% to 100%; a reported 7/11 low-effort result was withdrawn (11/11 on replication). Vendor paper with commercial interest. Gap check: the source abstract itself calls its surface unstable; a claimed v3.8 withdrawal was not found on the arXiv page.
agent_test: Pin model and date; replay a 3-level exception chain set several times and report variance before claiming any scaffold gain.

claim: An 'enhanced' prompt about revoked exemptions made things worse: net accuracy 89.7% to 64.7% (7 FN to 4 FN but 20 new false positives); baseline failures were identical across runs.
agent_test: Test any 'check exceptions' prompt for false-positive inflation, not only recall.

claim: Prompt format can swing a result by tens of points: GPT-5.4 on cuad_covenant_not_to_sue 53.9% few-shot (yes-rate 98.7%) vs 92.9% zero-shot; few-shot also helps weak models (+28.74 Llama 2 7B) and hurts strong ones (Opus -6.81).
schema_part: G (calibrate prompt format; no fixed few-shot)
agent_test: Run zero-shot vs few-shot per task type and check yes-rate bias before adopting exemplars.

claim: Default-exception abduction: strong LLMs write valid exception formulas (validity 96-100%) but not minimal ones (1-1.5 extra exceptions per world; gaps roughly double on holdout worlds); DeFAb finds over-broad exceptions delete valid predictions (34 of 36 L3 tasks). A symbolic verifier rejected 34 of 34 over-broad circular defeaters; no model-side held-out check has been tested.
schema_part: O (revise a rule: minimal exception) / G
agent_test: Score proposed exceptions on held-out cases; prefer the narrowest exception that fits.

claim: LLMs fail when conflicting rules have no priorities (levels-(5) wrong in 4 of 4 settings) and do better when priority rules or false-premise facts are supplied.
agent_test: Make rule priority explicit (specificity, recency, authority) and test with and without it.

claim: Argumentative scaffolds around LLMs give small, mixed gains: ArgLLM depth-1 with estimated base 0.81 vs direct 0.77 (StrategyClaim, Llama 3 8B); CQoT +4.61% reasoning, +5.4% math (GPT-4o judge); LOGicalThought +4.41% over best baseline. Gains depend on base score and judge. CQoT gains are 0.1-0.5 points on a 1-10 GPT-4o-judged scale, 40 questions, five models, no token accounting; Nemotron CoT beat CQoT on reasoning (7.7 vs 7.3).
agent_test: Implement critical-questions-of-thought as one operator; measure at equal tokens against self-consistency.

claim: Toulmin structure is elicited reliably from strong models (all three terms: GPT-4 99-100%) but falls for weaker ones (Falcon-40B 35-42.5%); presence of structure was measured, not whether it improves answers.
agent_test: Use Toulmin fields as output format; measure whether they change answer accuracy.

claim: Premise errors dominate step-by-step legal-style failures: accuracy-to-correctness drop averages 27%; 96% of chains from false premises contain a misinterpretation error; error-taxonomy feedback gives at most +4%.
agent_test: Add a premise verification step; measure correctness score, not final accuracy.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM legal-text formalisation results are sensitive to the evaluation: term identification F1 0.70-0.82; a prior reported F1 86.74% recomputed to 79.03%.
agent_test: Recompute any inherited metric ourselves before relying on it.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Late exceptions are the main LLM failure in belief updating: many models label an update as weakening yet keep the old conclusion (GPT-5-mini 95.4% labelled, 20.3% revised; GPT-5.1 default gap 0.935). Extended thinking nearly removes it in Qwen3-32B (gap 0.670 to 0.008). Order of questions matters (effect-first order changes scores by 0.3-0.7).
agent_test: Add a forced step: label each new fact as strengthen/weaken/neutral, then re-derive the verdict; test with question order swapped and 20 seeds.

claim: An explicit exception structure helps most on exception-active items and for weaker models, and can be neutral or negative elsewhere: LogT +4.41% over best baseline (up to +10 on 7-8B models, Claude 3.5 Haiku +0.5 to +2), but it costs about 21.5% more steps; NormBench gains concentrate on exception-active cases.
agent_test: Make the exception slot conditional, and compare to CoT at equal tokens.

claim: No direct LLM test of shifting burden of proof or proof standard exists in the sources found. Closest: LLM jurors gave higher guilt probability (63.56 vs 58.82) but fewer guilty verdicts (21% vs 49%) than humans, N=2,304 responses; a position paper proposes abstain/'unproven' flags and calibration metrics.
agent_test: Run a within-item test: same evidence, standard set to preponderance vs beyond reasonable doubt, measure verdict flips and probability thresholds.

claim: Rule-grounding is not guaranteed by accuracy: verdicts often stay the same when the governing rule is deleted, swapped or negated (general models 90-92% accurate; guard model 51%).
agent_test: Add a rule-swap probe to the trace tests.
